# FDG9156

> DO position the input buffer parameter (“source”) as the first method parameter, when there is an explicit input buffer parameter.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12.1 Data Transformation Operations.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9156
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Make the input buffer '{0}' the first parameter of '{1}'

The text has no body; the body of FDG9157 explains both. FDG9156 reports a parameter named source of an input buffer type (ReadOnlySpan<T>, ReadOnlyMemory<T>, ReadOnlySequence<T>, an array, ArraySegment<T> or string) of an externally visible method when a parameter before it is an output buffer named destination (an array can be either) or is neither another input buffer of those types nor an int that immediately follows an array (the array's offset), so that several source parameters may come first, as in the Xor example. A string or array named source is checked only when the method also has an output buffer (Span<T>, Memory<T>, an array or ArraySegment<T>), since without one it can be a name, a path or a collection; a ReadOnlySpan<T>, ReadOnlyMemory<T> or ReadOnlySequence<T> source is always checked. The this parameter of an extension method is not counted, as it stands for the instance of an instance method, which the body allows to provide the source. Input buffers with other names (left, nonce, plaintext), overrides and interface implementations are not checked, so coverage is partial. Span<T> and Memory<T> types need .NET Core 2.1 or later, or the System.Memory package on .NET Framework and .NET Standard 2.0 (see FDG9137). Reordering changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.
